newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW - First Bank loan mix raises charge-offs.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - First Bank loan mix raises charge-offs.

text.p: First Bank Systems Inc chief financial officer Richard Zona said Wednesday a rise in loan charge-offs in the third quarter reflects growth in the bank's loan portfolio and a change in the Minneapolis-based bank holding company's loan mix.

Net charge-offs were $42.7 million in the quarter, compared to $30 million a year ago and $36 million in the second quarter. Net charge-offs as a percent of average loans rose to 0.63 percent in the third quarter from 0.47 percent a year ago and 0.54 percent in the second quarter, $36.84 billion asset First Bank said.
"I don't expect it to come down in the perceivable future," Zona said in a telephone interview.
The Minneapolis-based bank's loan mix is shifting more to higher yielding credit card, home equity and small to middle market commercial loans from residential mortgage loans.
Also, average loans in the third quarter rose to $27.04 billion in the quarter from $25.88 billion a year ago.

Meanwhile, First Bank continued to show growing fee income while keeping costs down, reducing its efficiency ratio, or cost of raising revenue, to 49.8 percent before non-recurring items from 51.3 percent a year ago.
"We think there is still significant opportunity to lower the efficiency ratio," Zona said. "Our goal over the next few years is to get it to 45 percent."
Retail banking is the area were the most gains could be seen, through increased use of electronic banking channels, Zona said. But he added that other business lines can also yield efficiency gains.
In recent years, First Bank has exceeded its peer group in terms of efficiency ratio.

"Their peer group (efficiency) is probably more like the upper 50s," James Schutz, banking analyst at Chicago Corp said. "In terms of running an efficient shop, they're heads and shoulders above other banks."

He noted that gains the bank is making in fee income are important in decreasing that ratio. Credit card fees rose to $79.5 million in the third quarter from $62.7 million a year ago, while trust fees grew to $57.1 million from $42.8 million.

"Clearly, we are continuing to expand corporate trust through acquisitions," Zona said, adding that he expected more acquisition opportunities in that area as the trust industry consolidates. First Bank is also considering more acquisitions of full service banks, but "we will not dilute our current shareholders through acquisition."

First Bank shares fell 1/4 to 66-1/4 Wednesday after it reported third quarter earnings of $1.20 a share, before a one-time special assessment to refund the Savings Association Insurance Fund, compared with $1.06 a year ago. The earnings were one cent below the First Call median forecast.
